money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Mauritius Rupee (MUR). If you're travelling with more than MUR 500,000, you'll need to declare it when you arrive and depart. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. There are ATMs in most towns and in large shopping centres. You can use credit cards at most hotels, restaurants and large shops. Check with your bank if your cards will work in Mauritius.

laws.rule: Mauritius has severe penalties for drug offences, including fines and jail terms of up to 60 years. Pack all luggage yourself and do not carry anything through customs for anyone else. If you're found with any drugs, it’s unlikely you’ll be bailed, regardless of the type of drug. Prosecutions can take more than a year before going to court. You’ll be detained until your trial.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Mauritius has a zero-tolerance policy on alcohol consumption and driving. Penalties include licence suspension, heavy fines or imprisonment. In Mauritius, it's also illegal to: buy counterfeit or pirated goods own cigarette papers or rolling machines import, distribute or sell e-cigarettes smoke or vape in all indoor public places and some outdoor places.
laws.heading: Drink driving

laws.rule: Whilst same-sex relationships were decriminalised in October 2023, LGBTQIA+ people still face discrimination.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ travellers

laws.rule: To drive in Mauritius, you need to be at least 18 years old and have either: a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted); or an International Driving Permit (IDP) Obtain your IDP before leaving Australia.
laws.heading: Driver's license

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Mauritian society is conservative. Nudism is not permitted. Take care not to offend, especially if you visit: rural areas a shrine, temple, mosque or other religious site a religious event. At religious sites, cover your shoulders and knees, remove shoes in temples and mosques, and ask before photographing ceremonies.
